services.desc: This restored, original lunch counter, preserved in its historic location, represents an inflection point both for the revitalization of the Civil Rights Movement and the conversation of personal and social equity in America. On February 1, 1960, David Richmond, Frank McCain, Ezell Blair, Jr. (now Jibreel Khazan), and Joseph McNeil, now known as the Greensboro A&T Four - four college freshmen who attended N.C. Agricultural & Technical College - conducted a sit-in at a whites-only lunch counter in Greensboro.
